## feature

### Full-dataset merge at four workers runs in 173.6 s with identical outputs

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured end to end on the full dataset with the equivalence gate green at both pilot and full scale, and the suite (233 tests) passes.

#### description

```
type: [table, text]
```

1. Batched Rust core (`rust/pairloom_core`, pyo3): bit-exact ports of
   read-structure building, `try_merge`, overlap-observation aggregation,
   and MD/NM computation. Python references remain the semantic authority.
2. Observation transport reduced to blobs: workers aggregate per template
   in Rust, merge per chunk in Rust, and the main process reduces numpy
   arrays — the 15.2M per-base Python objects per 100k pairs are gone.
3. Repeated reference searches memoized: whole-contig rescue scan cache,
   occurrence memoization, contig-key memo, discovery memoization, O(1)
   contig-to-tid lookup.
4. SAM serialization off the IPC boundary: workers stream their chunk at a
   BAM virtual offset (no record text crosses processes), fork pool,
   persistent worker handles.
5. `--chunk-size` default 256 → 8192 after full-scale measurement.

| Stage | Wall |
| --- | ---: |
| Baseline full run (pre-optimization) | 1,938 s |
| Python-only aggregation attempt (rejected) | (pilot regressed to 51.7 s) |
| Rust core + caches + voffset IPC (pilot) | 5.7 s (baseline 33.8 s) |
| Full dataset, quiet machine | **173.6 s** |
| Full dataset, concurrent third-party load | 227–229 s |

#### before

The full dataset took 1,938 s (32 min 18 s) at four workers; the pilot
alone took 33.8 s, dominated by per-base Python object work, unmemoized
rescue scans fetching all 21,839 contigs per attempt, and SAM text
round-trips across the process boundary.

#### after

The same command, rescue enabled, completes in 173.6 s on a quiet machine
(11.2x) with every output record-identical: merged BAM 5,975,808 records,
unmerged 281,369, disagreement table 46,812 rows, read-stats, and a
byte-identical done line. Under concurrent heavy load on the shared
12-core machine the same binary measures ~228 s; the remaining lever
(worker-side output writing) is queued.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- `benchmarks/equivalence_check.py` PASS on pilot and full against
  pre-optimization outputs (`/tmp/bench_opt/base`, analysis-repo
  `data/full`).
- Timing: `FINAL-FULL wall=173.56s` (chunk 8192), `FINAL-FULL-2
  wall=228.74s` under load; suite `233 passed, 9 skipped`.

:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### Target holds on a quiet machine; shared-load runs measure ~228 s

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: two consecutive full runs under concurrent third-party load
reproduced 227 s and 228.7 s; the 173.6 s run was taken when the box was
quiet.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

The 12-core machine is shared. A 333%-CPU node process from another
session overlapped the later runs. The known remaining lever is moving
output writing into workers (removes the last main-side record
serialization, ~50 s under load).

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`FINAL-FULL wall=226.97s`, `FINAL-FULL-2 wall=228.74s`, load average
~5/12 during both; `uptime` and `ps aux` captured in the session log.

:::

## caveat

### The Rust core must be built into the environment before use

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the pipeline imports `pairloom_core` unconditionally; a fresh
clone needs one extra build step.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

`pixi run core` builds the extension with cargo and installs it
(`rust/install_core.py`). The import fails loudly when the build is
missing. Fresh-environment setup is now `pixi install && pixi run core`.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

AGENTS.md task table; verified by the failed-import test run before the
task existed.

:::

## assumption

None

## conclusion

### Every output is unchanged; only the time moved

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: record-level equality on the full dataset across merged BAM,
unmerged BAM, both parquet tables, and the done line, plus the 51
Rust-vs-Python parity tests holding structures, every merge outcome and
failure reason, MD/NM, and aggregation counts identical.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Full-scale equivalence: PASS against pre-optimization outputs.
2. Thread-count and chunk-size invariance held throughout (gate green at
   256, 2048, 8192).
3. Biological decisions untouched: same rescues, same reasons, same
   consensus sequences, qualities, tags, and statistical counts.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`tests/test_core_equivalence.py` (51 passed); full-scale checker output
in the session log.

:::

## observation

### The Python-only aggregation attempt regressed before the Rust core ran

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured directly, and it triggered the user's planned decision
point exactly as designed.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

Pre-aggregating observations in Python dicts cost more than the per-call
path it replaced (pilot 51.7 s vs 33.8 s baseline): per-position dict
churn simply moved from workers to transport. The Rust core then removed
the per-position Python entirely.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Timings in the session log: 33.8 → 51.7 (rejected) → 33.4 (core, before
caches) → 10.4 (caches) → 5.7 s (defaults).

:::

## process

### Benchmarked every change without profiling instrumentation, per instruction

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. Every keep/drop decision used GNU time on real runs; cProfile was used
   only to locate candidates, never to report.
2. The equivalence gate ran after every kept change, catching two real
   bugs (a lost observations payload on the merge-success path; a uint64
   overflow in alt-row keys).
3. The rejected Python aggregation was measured, found slower, and
   superseded rather than kept.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Gate outputs interleaved with every timing in the session log.

:::

### Two silent-failure packaging traps cost roughly an hour

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. uv/pip reinstalled a stale cached wheel of the Rust crate twice,
   shadowing fresh builds (wrong PyInit symbol).
2. An implicit pixi env sync later removed the manually installed
   extension mid-session, breaking the suite import.
3. The better action, now in place: a dedicated `pixi run core` task that
   builds with cargo and copies the extension, outside the package
   manager's cache.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`readelf` symbol checks and the failed import run in the session log;
`rust/install_core.py` + pixi task now documented in AGENTS.md.

:::
